Every member is on the queue and converged, so nothing in the slot mechanism is reachable any more — except through the callers listed below, which are the actual work.

Deliberately not started until #971 landed, because three of these callers were still live defects rather than dead code.

## Precondition (met)

All 12 adopted repos run the queue stub and have converged onto current canon. Deleting `run.mjs` strands any member whose workflow still calls it; none does.

## What actually dies

- `engine/scheduler/run.mjs` (636 lines) — the slot scheduler entry point
- `engine/scheduler/slots.mjs` — **only its slot half**: `dueSlots`, `FIRST_RUN_FREQUENCIES`, and the slot-id strings inside `mostRecentSlot`
- `engine/scheduler/stubs/claudinite-scheduler.yml` (94 lines) — the slot stub, and with it the `overrides` dispatch input
- `engine/scheduler/run-record.mjs`'s run-ledger half (`renderTaskRuns`, the watermark math)
- the slot-conformance checks in `packs/core/declared-checks.json`
- ~1,900 lines of slot-only tests (`run.test.mjs`, `slots.test.mjs`, `resolve-dispatch.test.mjs`, `run-record.test.mjs`, `signal-context.test.mjs`, `dispatch.test.mjs`)

## What must move first — this is not an `rm`

Four things the queue and the packs still genuinely need live inside the modules being deleted:

| what | lives in | needed by |
|---|---|---|
| `FREQUENCIES`, `DEFAULT_SCHEDULE`, `WEEKDAYS`, `normalizeSchedule`, the anchor arithmetic | `slots.mjs` | `queue/anchors.mjs`, `task-contract.mjs`, `packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs` |
| `buildSignalContext` | `run.mjs:313` | `queue/signals.mjs` |
| `ensureLabels` | `run.mjs` | `packs/basics/tasks/task-janitor/worker.mjs` |
| `parseOverrides` | `run.mjs` | `packs/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-digest/worker.mjs` |

Most of `slots.mjs` is calendar arithmetic with no slot identity in it. Suggested shape: rename `slots.mjs` → `calendar.mjs` carrying the frequency vocabulary and anchor instants (no ids), `buildSignalContext` → `signals/`, `ensureLabels` → `github.mjs`. Doing the extraction as a *separate earlier PR* would create a duplication window against the still-live `run.mjs`, so extraction and deletion belong in **one** change.

## The parameter plumbing — the real work

Four tasks take operator parameters through `CLAUDINITE_OVERRIDES`, the slot-era override bag:

- `sheepdog/fleet-baseline` — `REPOS`, `DRY_RUN`, `INCLUDE_DORMANT`
- `sheepdog/fleet-add-missing-packs` — `REPOS`, `ADD_PACKS`, `PACK_CONFIG`, `SCAN_FOR_NEEDED_PACKS`
- `sheepdog/fleet-digest` — `DIGEST_BACKFILL_DAYS`
- `core/adopt-requested-packs`

Under the queue, parameters ride the **item's Context**, and that path already exists: `prework-run.mjs` passes `CLAUDINITE_CONTEXT`. So each becomes a `create-work-item / --context "REPOS=…"`, and the workers swap which env var they parse — the `KEY=value` bag parser itself is unchanged, and `fleet-baseline`'s copy is already pack-local.

`fleet-digest` is the one to watch: merged in #958 *during* this migration, it added a fresh `parseOverrides` import from `run.mjs` and documents `FORCE_TASKS=fleet-digest` as its manual trigger. New slot-era callers are still arriving because the slot idiom is still the documented one, which is an argument for doing this soon rather than letting the surface grow again.

## Expect more of one class

Three defects so far were all "the flip changed a contract and its callers weren't swept":

| # | contract changed | caller left behind |
|---|---|---|
| #929 | the dispatch interface | Shepherd's fan-out tasks, sending `overrides` |
| #921 | the force recipe | DESIGN §8's own prose, omitting `task:ready` |
| #971 | forcing no longer bypasses the precondition | every `manual` task's precondition |

All three were invisible to Step 2's validation burst for the same structural reason: the burst exercised the queue's own paths, and each of these is a slot-era caller of a queue-era contract. Sweep for callers **outside** the module before deleting, and prefer a generic guard over a point fix each time one turns up — #971's guard quantifies over every declared task rather than naming the two that were broken.

## Done means

- [ ] the four helpers rehomed and their importers updated
- [ ] the four tasks take parameters via Context, with `FORCE_TASKS` gone from their docs and preconditions
- [ ] `run.mjs`, the slot half of `slots.mjs`, the slot stub, the ledger math and the slot-conformance checks deleted
- [ ] `grep -rn FORCE_TASKS` returns only historical citations (migration records, dated design docs)
- [ ] a forced `fleet-baseline` run observed converging a member end to end — the lever this whole thread exists to restore

input.title: #974 stranded fielded pack copies: the engine and pack lanes deliver separately, so a renamed engine module breaks the mount mid-converge
input.body:
Found by forcing Shepherd's converge immediately after #993 merged, which is exactly what that force is for. Shepherd's run went **green** and its stamp **did not move** — [run 32147342762](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32147342762), PR missingbulb/Shepherd#45 open and `needs-human`:

```
update: engine — needs-human: the converged tree FAILED its self-test
pack-manifests: the pack in packs/core failed to load:
  Cannot find module '.../.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/slots.mjs'
  imported from '.../.claudinite/shared/packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs'
```

## What is actually broken

The converged tree carries the **new engine** (`calendar.mjs`, no `slots.mjs`, no `run.mjs`) beside the **old `core` pack**, whose `task-declaration-shape.mjs` still imports `engine/scheduler/slots.mjs`.

That is not a race — it is the standing shape of the delivery model. The engine lane (`updates/engine-update.mjs`) and the pack lane (`updates/pack-update.mjs`) are separate PRs on separate cycles, and pack delivery is version-gated per pack. **There is always a window where a member has the new engine and an old pack**, and nothing can close it.

#974's precondition asked the right question of the wrong callers: *"deleting `run.mjs` strands any member whose workflow still calls it; none does."* True — but a **pack file** importing it strands the same way, and three do. Across every historical pack version the fielded imports are exactly:

| module | symbol | fielded importer |
|---|---|---|
| `slots.mjs` | `FREQUENCIES` | `packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs` |
| `run.mjs` | `ensureLabels` | `packs/basics/tasks/task-janitor/worker.mjs` |
| `run.mjs` | `parseOverrides` | `packs/sheepdog/tasks/fleet-digest/worker.mjs` |

The `core` one breaks the **mount** (a pack that fails to load fails the self-test, so the converge refuses to land at all). The other two would break their tasks at runtime.

## The fix

The repo already has this rule for the other direction — *"Changing an export in `updates/*` — empty it, never remove it. Fielded workers are stale callers of instantly-current flow modules"*. This is the same asymmetry one lane over: **fielded pack files are stale callers of an instantly-current engine.**

So `engine/scheduler/slots.mjs` and `engine/scheduler/run.mjs` come back as thin compatibility shims re-exporting only those three symbols, with an expiry condition stated at the definition: they go when no member's `packVersions` still names a version that imports them.

## Done means

- [ ] `slots.mjs` re-exports `FREQUENCIES` from `calendar.mjs`; `run.mjs` re-exports `ensureLabels` from `github.mjs` and `parseOverrides` from the bag parser
- [ ] a test that fails when either shim loses a symbol a fielded pack version imports — quantified over the imports found in git history, not a hand-kept list
- [ ] a guard that catches the general class: a `packs/**` file importing an `engine/**` module that this change deletes or renames
- [ ] Shepherd converges green, stamp moves, and PR missingbulb/Shepherd#45 is superseded
- [ ] only then the `fleet-baseline` `DRY_RUN` #974 still owes

input.body:
Closes #1004.

Forcing Shepherd's converge immediately after #993 merged found this — which is exactly what that force is for. The run went **green** and the stamp **did not move**: [run 32147342762](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/actions/runs/32147342762), PR missingbulb/Shepherd#45 open and `needs-human`.

```
pack-manifests: the pack in packs/core failed to load:
  Cannot find module '.../engine/scheduler/slots.mjs'
  imported from '.../packs/core/task-declaration-shape.mjs'
```

## The window nothing closes

The converged tree carried the **new engine** beside the **old `core` pack**. That is not a race — the engine lane and the pack lane are separate PRs on separate cycles, and pack delivery is version-gated per pack, so **every member spends a window holding the new engine and an old pack.**

A `packs/` file importing an `engine/` module is therefore a stale caller of an instantly-current engine. This repo already has the rule for the other lane — *"Changing an export in `updates/*` — empty it, never remove it"* — and this is the same asymmetry one lane over.

It is worse than a broken task: a pack that fails to load fails the mount's self-test, so the converge **refuses to land at all**, and the member cannot receive the pack version that would have fixed it. Self-healing is exactly what it takes away.

#974's precondition asked the right question of the wrong callers: *"deleting `run.mjs` strands any member whose workflow still calls it; none does."* True — three **pack files** import it.

## The fix

`slots.mjs` and `run.mjs` return as thin shims over `calendar.mjs` and `github.mjs`, carrying only what a fielded pack version imports, with the retirement condition stated at the definition (read members' stamped `packVersions`; don't guess a release).

`parseOverrides` is the one body that cannot re-export — its home is now a **pack**, and the engine may not import a pack. So it is duplicated, and the drift guard runs both copies over the same inputs rather than comparing text. Where they legitimately differ (the pack's parser ignores prose, because a work item's Context is prose first), the test asserts the difference instead of hiding it.

## The guard

`engine-tests/scheduler/engine-pack-lane-shims.test.mjs` derives which imports are fielded by walking the pack tree's history, so it needs no hand-kept list. Two things it learned the hard way, both pinned:

- **The trunk, not `--all`.** An import that only existed on an unmerged branch is not fielded. Scanning every ref fires on whatever is in flight — which it did on its first run, against #941's branch.
- **It refuses a shallow checkout.** With no history the scan finds nothing and reports clean — a green run proving nothing. CI uses `fetch-depth: 0`; the test now asserts that rather than assuming it.

Watched failing before green: removing either shim turns it red with the module named.

## Verification

2072 tests pass; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The lesson is in the canon's local pack, beside the `updates/*` rule it generalizes.

Shepherd re-converges once this lands, which supersedes its #45 — and only then is #974's outstanding `fleet-baseline` `DRY_RUN` meaningful, since Shepherd's vendored worker still reads the old channel until it converges.
